issues.description: The problem statement and UML require Farm.animals to be a List<Animal> and explicitly instruct students to implement it using an ArrayList (preserving insertion order). The reference solution, however, implements animals as a Set<Animal> (HashSet). This is a structural mismatch: it changes the collection type/API and the iteration ordering semantics (HashSet is unordered), which can confuse students about which collection to use and may cause different behavior in singFarmSong() and tests that assume List/ArrayList semantics.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the reference solution with the problem specification: change the Farm implementation to use List<Animal> (e.g., ArrayList<Animal>) for the animals attribute, update the getter/setter signatures accordingly, and initialize animals = new ArrayList<>() in the no-arg constructor. Ensure singFarmSong() iterates the List so verse order is deterministic and matches the intended behavior.

issues.description: The problem statement explicitly requires the Farm to hold its animals in a List implemented with an ArrayList, but the solution implementation uses a Set (HashSet) for the same conceptual entity (the collection of animals). This divergence between the requested collection type (List/ArrayList) and the solution's collection type (Set/HashSet) creates a mapping confusion for students who are instructed to use an ArrayList in the exercise text but will find a different collection type in the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement by changing the Farm implementation to use List<Animal> and initialize it with new ArrayList<>() (and corresponding getter/setter types), or alternatively update the problem statement to accept a Set/HashSet and clearly explain the reason for using a Set. Prefer making the solution use List/ArrayList to match the exercise instructions.
